Rashi on Shabbat 3a:1:1.hebrew: בבא דרישא - העני חייב ובעל הבית פטור, ובעל הבית חייב והעני פטור, דפטור מחטאת ומותר לכתחלה, דהא לאו עקירה עבד ולא הנחה עבד, [שהאחר] הניחה בידו:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:1:1.english: The clause of the first section - [Namely,] "the poor person is liable and the homeowner is exempt," and "the homeowner is liable and the poor person is exempt" — for [the one who is exempt] is exempt from a sin-offering and [the action is] permitted ab initio, since he did not perform an uprooting and he did not perform a placing, [as the other person] placed it into his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:2:1.hebrew: פטור אבל אסור - פטור מחטאת, אבל אסור מדבריהם לכתחלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:2:1.english: Exempt but forbidden - [One is] exempt from a sin offering, but [it is] forbidden rabbinically ab initio.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:2:2.hebrew: צידת צבי וצידת נחש ומפיס מורסא - כולהו בפ' ר"א אומר האורג בסיפיה, והתם מפרש טעמייהו, מנא ליה בהו דפטור ומותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:2:2.english: Trapping a deer, and trapping a snake, and lancing an abscess - All of them are [discussed] at the end of the chapter "Rabbi Eliezer says: One who weaves," and there [the Gemara] explains their reasons: from where he [Shmuel] derives regarding them that [one is] exempt and [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:2:3.english: An abscess - Cuisture in Old French [an abscess].

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:2:4.english: One who drains - Squeezes [it] so that it will open and the pus will come out.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:3:1.hebrew: כי איצטריכא ליה - לאשמעינן דפטור ומותר בהנך דאית בהו מעשה, כגון הני תלת, ותו ליכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:3:1.english: When it was necessary for him - [It was] to teach us that [cases of] "exempt and permitted" among those that involve an action are such as these three, and there are no more.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:3:2.english: There are many - Such as those of the first clause [of the Mishnah].

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:4:1.hebrew: פטורי דאתי בהו לידי חיוב חטאת - כגון עקירות, שהן תחלת המלאכה, דאיכא למגזר דילמא גמר לה. אבל הנחות לא מצי למיתי לידי חיוב חטאת, דהא ליכא עקירה גבי האי. וארבע דקתני בכל חד - תרתי דחיובא, ועקירה דפטורא דתרתי נינהו: פשט העני ידו מלאה לפנים - הא חדא, או שנתן לתוכה בע"ה וידו של עני היתה ריקנית - הא תרתי, וכן באידך. ורבותי' אומרים: פשיטות יד לפנים [לגבי שניהם], בין מלאה בין ריקנית, היא תחלת המעשה, וההוא הוא דקחשיב, דהוו להו תרתי בעני ותרתי בבע"ה. כל חיוב ופטור במסכת שבת - בחטאת קאי, ובשוגג:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:4:1.english: Exempt cases through which one could come to liability for a sin-offering - Such as [acts of] uprooting, which are the beginning of the labor, where there is [reason] to decree lest he complete it. But [acts of] placing cannot come to lead to liability for a sin-offering, for there is no uprooting in the case of this [person]. And the "four" that [the Mishnah] teaches for each one are: two of liability, and [acts of] uprooting of exemption, which are two: The poor person extended his hand full inside — that is one; or the homeowner placed [an object] into it when the poor person's hand was empty — that is two; and so too in the other [clause]. And my teachers say: Extending a hand inside [regarding both of them], whether full or empty, is the beginning of the action, and that is what [the Mishnah] counts, so that there are two for the poor person and two for the homeowner. Every [instance of] liability and exemption in tractate Shabbat refers to a sin-offering, and [applies to one who acted] unwittingly.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:5:1.english: From the people of the land when he does it - It is written regarding a sin-offering.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:1.hebrew: הטעינו חבירו - שהיה גופו ברה"י, והטעינו חבירו, דאיהו גופיה לא עקר מידי:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:1.english: His fellow loaded him - That his body was in the private domain and his fellow loaded him, so that he himself did not lift anything.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:2.hebrew: אוכלין ומשקין - אורחא דמילתא נקט, דבר הצריך לשבת, ודרך בני אדם להתעסק בהן בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:2.english: Food and drink - [He] mentioned the common case: an item needed for Shabbat, and it is the way of people to handle them on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:3.english: The moving of his body - That he moved his feet from the house after he was loaded.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:4.hebrew: ואינו דומה לידו - הפשוטה לפנים וגופו לחוץ, ונתן בע"ה לתוכה, דפטור ביה תנא דמתני' אף לעני שהוציאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:4.english: And it is not similar to his hand - [Which is] extended inside while his body is outside, and the homeowner placed [an object] into it, where the Tanna of our Mishnah exempts even the poor person who carried it out.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:5.hebrew: ידו לא נייח - הלכך כי הוציאה, לא עקר מידי, ואין דרך הוצאה בלא עקירה והנחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:5.english: His hand is not at rest - Therefore, when he brought it [his hand] out, he did not uproot anything, and the manner of carrying out is not without an uprooting and a setting down.

Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:6.hebrew: גופו נייח - ע"ג קרקע, והויא עקירה. ל"א: "ידו בתר גופו גרירא" — ל"ג, דיתירא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 3a:6:6.english: His body is at rest - [His body rests] upon the ground, and [therefore moving it] is an akirah [an act of lifting]. Another version: "His hand is drawn after his body" — we do not read [this], because it is superfluous.

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:1:1.hebrew: בבא דרישא פטור ומותר - וא"ת: והא קא עבר אלפני עור לא תתן מכשול? ואפילו מיירי שהיה יכול ליטלו אפילו לא היה בידו, דלא עבר משום לפני עור, דמושיט כוס יין לנזיר מוקי לה בפ"ק דמס' עבודת כוכבים (דף ו:) דקאי בתרי עברי דנהרא, מ"מ איסור דרבנן מיהא איכא, שחייב להפרישו מאיסור. ואפילו אי מיירי בנכרי, דלא שייך לפני עור, מיהו איסור דרבנן מיהא איכא, כדתניא בשילהי פירקין (דף יט.): נותנין מזונות לנכרי בחצר, נטלו ויצא, אין נזקקין לו, משמע דווקא כשהנכרי בחצר, אבל אם עומד בחוץ ופושט ידו לפנים, משמע דאסור ליתן להדיא ע"מ להוציא. ויש לומר: דמיירי בנכרי והחפץ של נכרי, דאפילו מכניס ומוציא כל היום אין כאן איסור כלל, כיון שאין החפץ של בעל הבית:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:1:1.english: The first clause [is] exempt and permitted - And if you say: But isn't he violating [the prohibition], "You shall not place a stumbling block before the blind" (lifnei iver)? And even if [one were to suggest that] we are dealing with [a case where] he was able to take it even if it were not in his hand - so that he does not violate [the Torah prohibition] on account of lifnei iver, as [the case of] handing a cup of wine to a nazirite (nazir) is established in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (6b) as [referring specifically to] where they are standing on two opposite banks of a river (trei ivrei denahara) - nevertheless, there is at least a rabbinic prohibition (issur derabbanan), for one is obligated to separate him from sin. And even if we are dealing with a gentile (nochri), to whom lifnei iver does not apply, nonetheless there is at least a rabbinic prohibition, as it is taught at the end of our chapter (19a): "One may give food to a gentile in a courtyard; if he took it and went out, one does not need to attend to him" - which implies [that this is permitted] specifically when the gentile is in the courtyard, but if he is standing outside and extending his hand inside, this implies that it is forbidden to give [it to him] explicitly on condition to carry [it] out. And one can say that we are dealing with a gentile, and the object belongs to the gentile, for [in that case] even if he brings [it] in and takes [it] out all day, there is no prohibition here at all, since the object does not belong to the homeowner (baal habayit).

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:2:1.hebrew: בר מהני תלת - הקשה ר"ת: הא איכא הא דתנן בפרק במה מדליקין (לקמן שבת כט:) המכבה את הנר מפני שהוא מתירא כו', ואם בשביל החולה שיישן פטור, ומוקי לה בחולה שיש בו סכנה, וא"כ הוא פטור ומותר, דאין לך דבר שעומד בפני פקוח נפש. ותירץ, דהא מלתא דפשיטא היא, ולא איצטריך ליה לשמואל לאשמעי', כדמשני בסמוך דלא איצטריך ליה לאשמעי' פטורי דלא קעביד מעשה. וצד נחש מיירי בדליכא סכנה, שיוכל להנצל בענין אחר, אלא משום צערא שרו ליה רבנן, כמו במפיס מורסא. וכן מוכח בריש פרק שמונה שרצים (שם קז:), דצד נחש לאו משום סכנה פטור, דהא מוקי לה כר"ש, דאמר מלאכה שאצ"ל פטור עליה. וע"ק לר"י: והא איכא הא דתני' בפ' במה אשה (שבת סב.) ר"א פוטר בכובלת ובצלוחית של פלייטון, והוא פטור ומותר, דהא בבריי' אחרת קתני התם: רא"א יוצאה אשה בכובלת לכתחלה? ותירץ ר"י בשם ר' אברהם, דלא חשיב שמואל אלא פטורים השנויין במשנה: דצד צבי משנה היא בהאורג (שם ד' קו:), הצד נחש ומפיס מורסא משנה היא בעדיות (פ"ב מ"ה). ולספרים דגרסי בפ' במה אשה (שבת ד' סב.): איידי דאמר ר"מ חייב חטאת א"ל איהו פטור אבל אסור, פי' דר"א קאמר לר"מ: לדבריך נמי לכל היותר לא יהא אלא פטור אבל אסור — לפי גרסא זו אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:2:1.english: Except for these three - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: But isn't there that which we learned in a mishna in the chapter "Bameh Madlikin" (below, Shabbat 29b): "One who extinguishes a lamp because he is afraid, etc., and if [he extinguished it] on account of a sick person so that he may sleep, he is exempt"? And [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to a dangerously ill person (choleh she-yesh bo sakanah). And if so, he is exempt and permitted (patur umutar), for there is nothing that stands in the way of saving a life (pikuach nefesh)! And he answered that this matter is obvious, and Shmuel did not need to teach it to us, just as [the Gemara] resolves nearby that he did not need to teach [cases of] exemption where one does not perform an action. And [as for] trapping a snake, it is dealing with [a case] where there is no danger [to life], as he could save himself in another manner; rather, on account of [preventing] pain, the Rabbis permitted it to him, just as in [the case of] draining an abscess. And so it is proven at the beginning of the chapter "Shemonah Sheratzim" (ibid. 107b), that one who traps a snake is exempt not on account of danger, for it establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says that for a labor not needed for its own sake (melachah she-einah tzerichah le-gufah) one is exempt. And furthermore, Ri raised a difficulty: But isn't there that which is taught in a baraita in the chapter "Bameh Ishah" (Shabbat 62a): Rabbi Eliezer exempts regarding a perfume basket (kovelet) and regarding a flask of balsam oil (tzelochit shel palyetun)? And this [ruling of "exempt"] means exempt and permitted, for in another baraita it teaches there: "Rabbi Eliezer says: A woman may go out [wearing] a perfume basket ab initio (lechatchila)"! And Ri answered in the name of Rabbi Avraham that Shmuel counted only exemptions that are taught in a mishna: for "trapping a deer" is a mishna in "HaOreg" (ibid. 106b); "one who traps a snake" and "one who drains an abscess" is a mishna in Eduyot (2:5). And according to the texts that read in the chapter "Bameh Ishah" (Shabbat 62a): "Since Rabbi Meir said [she is] liable to a sin-offering, [Rabbi Eliezer] said to him: [she is] exempt but forbidden" — meaning that Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Meir: "Even according to your words, at most it should only be exempt but forbidden" — according to this reading, it works out well.

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:2:2.hebrew: הצד נחש - הקשה בה"ג דשמואל אדשמואל: דהכא סבר שמואל מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה פטור כר"ש, ומשום צערא דגופא שרי. ובפ' כירה (ל מן מב.) אמרינן: בדבר שאין מתכוין סבר לה כר"ש, במלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה סבר לה כר"י. ותירץ ר"ת, דשמואל קאמר: דלר"ש, דאמר מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה פטור, בהני תלת פטור ומותר, כמו שמוכיח שמואל בסוף האורג (שם ק'.) דודאי פטור ומותר קאמר, וליה לא ס"ל כר"ש. ומיהו לדידן קי"ל כר"ש, דרבא דהוי בתראה סבר כותיה בריש נוטל (שבת קמא:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:2:2.english: One who traps a snake - The Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot (Behag) raised a contradiction between [one statement of] Shmuel and [another statement of] Shmuel: for here Shmuel holds [that for] a labor not needed for its own sake (melakhah she-einah tzerikhah legufah), one is exempt (patur) in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, and on account of bodily distress (tza'ara degufa) it is permitted [ab initio]; whereas in the chapter "Kirah" (below, 42a) we say that regarding an unintentional act (davar she-eino mitkavein) he holds like Rabbi Shimon, [but] regarding a labor not needed for its own sake he holds like Rabbi Yehuda [that one is liable]. And Rabbeinu Tam answered that Shmuel is saying that according to Rabbi Shimon—who says that [for] a labor not needed for its own sake one is exempt—in these three [cases] it is exempt and permitted (patur umutar), just as Shmuel proves at the end of "HaOreg" (there, 107a) that it certainly means "exempt and permitted"; but he himself does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. However, for us, we hold in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, for Rava, who is a later authority (batra'ah), holds like him at the beginning of "Notel" (Shabbat 141b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:2:3.hebrew: ומפיס מורסא - בעדיות (פ"ב שם) תנן: אם לעשות לה פה חייב, ואם להוציא ממנה ליחה פטור. וא"ת: היכי מתחייב אפתיחת פה דמורסא, הא אמרינן לקמן בפ' חבית (שבת ד' קו.): כל פתח שאינו עשוי להכניס ולהוציא אינו פתח? ותירץ ר"ת, דהאי נמי עשוי להכניס אויר ולהוציא ליחה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:2:3.english: And one who lances an abscess - In Eduyot (chapter 2, ibid.) we learned [in a Mishnah]: If [it is] to make an opening for it, he is liable; but if [it is] to extract pus from it, he is exempt. And if you say: How is one liable for opening an aperture in an abscess, seeing that we say below in the chapter "Chavit" (Shabbat 106a): "Any opening that is not made [both] to let in and to let out is not [considered] an opening"? And Rabbeinu Tam answers that this [opening], too, is made to let in air and to let out pus.

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:4:1.hebrew: פטורי דאתי לידי חיוב חטאת - מה שפירש"י דעקירות קחשיב, אינו נראה לר"י: חדא, דעקירה בלא הוצאה אינה אלא טלטול בעלמא, ואין בה דררא דחיוב חטאת כלל. ועוד, דלפי' הקונט' קחשיב לבע"ה ג' יציאות והכנסה אחת, ולעני ג' הכנסות והוצאה אחת. ועוד, דלא חשיב תרתי לפטור, דעני באחת ודעשיר באחת, כדחשיב חיובא ברישא. ומפרש ריב"א, דאתי לידי חיוב חטאת היינו אותו שפושט את ידו ומכניסה או מוציאה, דכוותה בבא דרישא חייב חטאת, והכא פטור, לפי שלא עשה כל המלאכה, שחיסר ממנה מעט: או עקירה או הנחה. והביא ראייה מירושלמי, דקאמר: לא אתיא מתני' אלא פטור שנגד החיוב. ומשום הכי לא חשיב אלא פטור של אותו שכנגדו חייב למעלה בבבא דרישא, כגון פשט העני את ידו לפנים כו' וקתני העני חייב, פטורה דידיה חשיב בבבא דסיפא בפשט העני את ידו לפנים וכו', וכן לבע"ה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:4:1.english: Exemptions that can lead to liability for a sin-offering - That which Rashi explained, that [the Tanna] is counting uprootings (akirot), does not seem correct to the Ri. First, an uprooting without carrying out is merely moving [an object in place] (tiltul be'alma), and has no connection to liability for a sin-offering at all. And furthermore, according to the explanation of the Kuntres (Rashi), [the Mishnah] would be counting for the homeowner three [acts of] carrying out (yetzi'ot) and one [act of] bringing in (hachnasah), and for the poor person three [acts of] bringing in and one [act of] carrying out. And furthermore, it does not count two [cases of] exemption—that of the poor person in one [clause] and that of the homeowner in one [clause]—as it counts liability in the first clause (reisha). And the Riva explains that [exemptions that] "can lead to liability for a sin-offering" refers to that [person] who extends his hand and brings it in or takes it out, where in the corresponding case in the first clause (reisha) he is liable for a sin-offering, but here he is exempt because he did not perform the entire labor, as he lacked a little of it: either the uprooting (akirah) or the placing (hanachah). And he brought proof from the Yerushalmi, which states: The Mishnah comes only [to teach] an exemption that corresponds to liability. And on this account, it counts only the exemption of that [person] who in the corresponding case above in the first clause (reisha) is liable—for example, [where] "the poor person extended his hand inside, etc.," and it teaches "the poor person is liable," it is his exemption that it counts in the latter clause (seifa) in [the case where] "the poor person extended his hand inside, etc."; and similarly for the homeowner.

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:5:1.hebrew: שניהם פטורין והא איתעבידא מלאכה מבינייהו - אינו קאי אמתני', שהרי רישא דשניהם פטורין, דהיינו פשט העני את ידו לפנים, קבעי לקמן (שבת ד' ד.). אלא קאי אמאי דקאמר: פטורי דאתי בהו לידי חיוב חטאת קחשיב, אבל חטאת לית בהו אלא שניהן פטורין כדקתני מתני'. ואמאי? והא איתעבידא מלאכה מבינייהו! ולא פריך שיתחייב הראשון, דאין סברא דע"י השני שעשה הנחה וגמר המלאכה יתחייב הראשון. אלא אשני קא פריך שיתחייב, לפי שעל ידו נגמרה המלאכה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:5:1.english: Both of them are exempt; but wasn't a labor performed between them? - This does not refer to the Mishnah, for the first clause [of cases where] "both of them are exempt" — namely, [where] the poor person extended his hand inside — it inquires about below (Shabbat 4a). Rather, it refers to what it [just] stated: "it counts exemptions where one can come through them to liability for a sin-offering (chatat)." But there is no sin-offering [liability] in them; rather, "both of them are exempt," as the Mishnah teaches! And why [are they exempt]? Wasn't a labor performed between them?! And it is not objecting that the first person should be liable, for there is no reason [to think] that through the second person, who performed the placement (hanachah) and completed the labor, the first person should become liable. Rather, it is objecting regarding the second person, that he should be liable, since it was through him that the labor was completed.

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:5:2.hebrew: בעשותה - בכל הספרים גר': העושה את כולה ולא העושה מקצתה, יחיד שעשה אותה חייב, שנים שעשאוה פטורין. פשטיה דקרא נראה דבעשותה קאי אנפש, אבל הש"ס דריש ליה אמלאכה, כלומר: בעשות אותה. וכולה מיירי בזה עוקר וזה מניח, ואינו אלא כפל מלה. וליכא למימר דב' שעשאוה איירי בב' שעשאוה בבת אחת, דבפרק המצניע (לקמן שבת צג. ושם) משמע דצריכי תרי קראי לזה עוקר וזה מניח ולב' שעשו מלאכה בבת אחת. ועוד, דבאיתמר נמי דקאי אמתניתין נמי קאמר האי לישנא: יחיד ועשה אותה וכו'. אך קשה, דבפרק המצניע (שם.) משמע דזה עוקר וזה מניח נפקא מנפש או מאחת, והכא נפקא לה מבעשותה. קשה לר"י: מדמצרכינן קרא לפטור, משמע דזה עוקר וזה מניח היה במשכן. ובפרק המצניע (ג"ז שם.) נמי פוטר ר"ש זה אינו יכול וזה אינו יכול, אע"פ שהיה במשכן, כגון ב' שנושאין את הארון. ובירושלמי פרק הזורק, אהא דתנן: שתי גזוזטראות ברשות הרבים כו' היו שתיהן בדיוטא אחת המושיט חייב, אמר רב חמא בשם ר' מיישא: ובלבד על ידי ב', ופריך: בכל אתר אמרת ב' שעשאוה פטורין, וכאן אמרת חייבין? ומשני: שכך היתה עבודת הלוים. והשתא, מה בכך שהיתה במשכן? מ"מ הוי ליה לפטור מושיט, כיון דשניהם עושין אותה! ונראה לר"י, דבמושיט אין זה עוקר וזה מניח, אלא המושיט עשה עקירה והנחה. ולא קשיא ליה בירושלמי אלא אמה שאינו פטור, ובכל מקום על ידי חבירו פטור [טפי], כגון ב' שעשאוה, וכאן אינו מתחייב אלא על ידי חבירו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:5:2.english: When she does it - In all books the text reads: "One who performs all of it and not one who performs part of it; an individual who performed it is liable, two who performed it are exempt." The plain meaning of the verse appears to be that "be'asotah" refers to the soul (nefesh) [i.e., when she does it], but the Talmud expounds it [as referring] to the labor (melakhah), that is to say: in doing it. And the entire [baraita] is dealing with [a case where] this one uproots and that one places down (zeh oker vezeh mani'ach), and it is merely a repetition of words [for emphasis]. And one cannot say that "two who performed it" is dealing with two [people] who performed it simultaneously (be-vat achat), for in the chapter "HaMatznea" (below, Shabbat 93a and there) it implies that two verses are needed: [one] for [the case where] this one uproots and that one places down, and [one] for two who performed a labor simultaneously. And furthermore, in the statement introduced by "It was also stated" (Itamar) as well, which refers to our mishna, it also uses this phrasing: "an individual who performed it, etc." However, this is difficult, for in the chapter "HaMatznea" (ibid.) it implies that [the exemption for] this one uproots and that one places down is derived from "nefesh" or from "achat", whereas here it derives it from "be'asotah"! Ri raises a difficulty: Since we require a verse to exempt [them], this implies that [the scenario of] this one uproots and that one places down existed in the Mishkan! And in the chapter "HaMatznea" (also there, 93a), Rabbi Shimon also exempts [in a case where] this one is incapable and that one is incapable [of doing it alone] (zeh eino yakhol vezeh eino yakhol), even though it existed in the Mishkan, such as two [people] carrying the Ark. And in the Yerushalmi, in the chapter "HaZorek" [11:2], regarding that which we learned: "[If there were] two balconies in the public domain, etc., [if] they were both on the same story, one who passes [an object from one to the other] is liable" — Rav Chama said in the name of Rabbi Meisha: "Provided [it is done] by means of two [people]." And it objects: "Everywhere else you say that [if] two performed it they are exempt, and here you say they are liable?!" And it answers: "Because such was the service of the Levites." And now, what of it that it was in the Mishkan? Nevertheless, [the Torah] should exempt one who passes, since both of them are performing it! And it seems to Ri that in the case of one who passes, this is not [a case of] this one uproots and that one places down; rather, the one who passes performed [both] the uprooting (akirah) and the placing down (hanachah). And the Yerushalmi was troubled only by why he is not exempt, given that everywhere else [performing a labor] by means of one's fellow makes one exempt [even more so], as in [the case of] two who performed it [together], whereas here he becomes liable only by means of his fellow.

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:5:3.hebrew: איתמר נמי כו' - תימה, דמייתי סייעתא משמעתא לברייתא, ובפרק קמא דקדושין (ד' ו.) פריך: "יהודה ועוד לקרא?". וי"ל, ד"נזרקה מפי חבורה" דקאמר, היינו חבורה של תנאים. ור"י תירץ, משום דבריי' דלעיל לא מתניא בי ר' חייא ור' אושעיא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:5:3.english: It was also stated, etc. - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] brings support from an amoraic teaching (shema'ata) for a baraita, when in the first chapter of Kiddushin (6a) it challenges: "[Does the custom of] Judea [serve as] 'and furthermore' to Scripture?!" [i.e., questioning whether Scripture requires corroboration from Judean custom — so why should an authoritative baraita need corroboration from an Amora?]. And one can say that when [Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda] said "it emanated from the group," this refers to a group of Tannaim [so it was a tannaitic tradition supporting a baraita, not an amoraic one]. And the Ri answered that [corroboration was needed] because the baraita above was not taught in the academy of Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Oshaya [and therefore required support].

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:6:1.hebrew: עקירת גופו כעקירת חפץ דמי או לא - נראה לר"י, דהכי נמי מצי למיבעי לענין הנחה, כגון שהוציא חפץ לר"ה ועמד שם לפוש, ולא הניחו ע"ג קרקע, אם הנחת גופו הוה כהנחת חפץ או לא. וממתני' דקתני: או שנטל מתוכה והוציא, העני חייב - ליכא למיפשט, דאיכא לאוקמא שהניחו ע"ג קרקע. וא"ת: ואמאי לא פשיט ממתניתין (ד' יא:) דקתני: לא יצא החייט במחטו שמא ישכח ויצא? ואי עקירת גופו לאו כעקירת חפץ דמי, אמאי לא יצא בה? הא לא מצי למיתי לידי איסור דאוריי'! וי"ל, דאפ"ה אסרו רבנן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:6:1.english: Is the uprooting of his body considered like the uprooting of an object, or not - It seems to the Ri that he could also have asked [this dilemma] regarding placing (hanachah), such as where one carried an object out into the public domain (reshut harabim) and stopped there to rest, but did not place it on the ground - [namely,] whether the coming to rest of his body is considered like the placing of an object, or not. And from our Mishnah, which teaches: "or if he took [an object] from inside it and brought it out, the poor person is liable" - this cannot be resolved, as it can be established [as referring to a case] where he placed it on the ground. And if you say: But why doesn't he resolve [the dilemma] from the Mishnah (11b), which teaches: "A tailor may not go out with his needle [near nightfall], lest he forget and go out [on Shabbat]"? For if the uprooting of his body is not considered like the uprooting of an object, why shouldn't he go out with it? Behold, he cannot come to [transgress] a biblical prohibition! And one can say that even so, the Sages prohibited [it].

Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:6:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא ידו לא נייח - נראה לר"י כלשון אחר דגרס: ידו, דבתר גופו גרירא, בעי עקירה, גופו לא בעי עקירה. ולמאי דגרס נמי "ידו לא נייח", מפרש ר"י דהיינו משום דבתר גופו גריר. ורש"י פי' ידו לא נייח ע"ג קרקע, משמע אפי' הוא וידו במקום אחד, ונתן לו חבירו לתוך ידו והוציא — פטור. ואין נראה, דבכל ענין שהטעינו חבירו, בין על כתפו בין על ידו, והוציא — חייב, דהא קתני: או שנטל מתוכה והוציא חייב, אלמא הנחת חפץ ביד בע"ה, שהוא וידו ברשות אחת, הויא הנחה, מדחייב העני שעקר מיד בע"ה. וכיון דהויא הנחה, כשעוקר גופו עם זה שבידו — הרי עוקרו ממקום הנחה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 3a:6:2.english: What is the reason his hand is not at rest - It seems to the Ri [that the correct explanation is] in accordance with the other version [of the text], which reads: "His hand, which is dragged after his body, requires an [independent] uprooting; his body does not require an uprooting." And even according to the version that reads "his hand is not at rest," the Ri explains that this is because it is dragged after his body. And Rashi explained: "his hand is not at rest" [means not at rest] upon the ground. This implies that even if he and his hand are in the same place, and his fellow placed [an object] into his hand and he carried it out, he is exempt. But this does not seem right, for in any case where his fellow loaded [an object] upon him, whether onto his shoulder or into his hand, and he carried it out, he is liable. For behold, it is taught [in the mishna, Shabbat 2a]: "or if [the poor person] took [an item] from within it and carried it out, [he is] liable." Evidently, placing an object in the hand of the homeowner (ba'al habayit), when he and his hand are in one domain, constitutes a [valid] placement (hanachah), since the poor person who uprooted [it] from the hand of the homeowner is liable. And since it constitutes a [valid] placement, when he uproots his body together with that which is in his hand, behold, he uproots it from a place of placement (makom hanachah).
